subject: HIPAA: BAA availability & PHI handling — deployment options

Cc: rishi_malhotra, dev_patel, monica_patel

Subject: HIPAA: BAA availability & PHI handling — deployment options

Hi Alice and Tom —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we all have alignment on HIPAA/PHI handling and deployment eligibility.

Summary from today's call:
- St. Martin Health will be sending ePHI to the inference service (patient names, DOB, limited clinical notes) for a clinical summarization workflow.
- Primary concerns: BAA execution, PHI boundaries (what is persisted), log retention, and which Redwood deployment modes are eligible to process PHI.

Redwood position (high level):
- We can execute a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) for customers that run workloads on Dedicated reserved capacity with private networking (VPC) or on our Private deployment options (customer-managed VPC or on-prem).
- Our hosted, shared multitenant API (public hosted) is not permitted for PHI/ePHI under Redwood policy.
- Audit & attestation: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II; I can attach the latest SOC 2 report under NDA.

PHI handling details (summary — engineering follow-up below):
- Logging: we support configurable logging; Dedicated + Private deployments can opt into disabled request/response logging and reduced telemetry by default.
- KV cache: kept in-memory; no persistent dumps unless explicitly enabled.
- Encryption: data-in-transit and at-rest with customer-managed KMS options for Dedicated/Private.

Proposed next steps:
1) I attached a draft BAA (BAA_Draft_Redwood_v1.pdf). Please review and mark up. We typically sign BAAs for Dedicated/VPC and Private deployments.
2) Tom — can you confirm whether you plan to send PHI to inference in production or for prototyping only?
3) We'll kick off the security questionnaire — copying ShieldSec for the technical responses and our SE (dev_patel) to schedule an architecture review.
4) If acceptable, let's schedule a 30-min architecture call next week to confirm network/keys and logging settings.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call any time.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Subject: Re: HIPAA: BAA availability & PHI handling — deployment options

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifying questions before we loop in procurement/legal: 

1) PHI boundary: in our use case, the inference requests will include patient identifiers and short clinical notes. Will Redwood ever persist the full request text outside transient memory? In particular, are there request logs or telemetry that will contain PHI by default?

2) Deployment options: you mentioned Dedicated (VPC) and Private/on-prem as eligible. Is Dedicated with a customer VPC and customer-managed KMS sufficient for HIPAA (i.e., we don't have to go full on-prem unless we need it)?

3) SOC 2: can you confirm the dated SOC 2 attestation (Type II) you referenced and how we can get a copy? Legal will want that before signing the BAA.

We'd like to move quickly — the initial plan is a pilot with production-like data.

Regards,
Tom Rivera
Director of IT Security | St. Martin Health
tom.rivera@stmartinshealth.org

Tom/Marissa/Alice —

Looping in a short technical summary to address Tom's questions. Happy to walk through in the architecture call.

1) Persistence & logging:
- By default our shared hosted API captures request/response logs and telemetry; that environment is not approved for PHI.
- For Dedicated (private VPC) and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, we offer a "no-logging" configuration that prevents request/response persistence to our centralized logs. That is a standard option when we sign a BAA.
- KV cache is in-memory and used for inference performance; it is not written to disk in typical configurations. We can enable a fully ephemeral-mode where caches are zeroed on instance termination and never written to persistent storage.

2) Deployment eligibility:
- Dedicated with VPC and customer-managed KMS is generally acceptable for HIPAA workloads and is the most common path for customers who want isolation but still use Redwood-managed control plane features.
- Private (customer-managed on-prem or private control plane in their VPC) is available for maximum isolation and is also supported under our BAA.
- Hosted/shared multitenant API is explicitly disallowed for PHI.

3) SOC 2 and attestation:
- We have a current SOC 2 Type II report (Nov 2025 coverage). We'll provide the report under NDA — I can upload to a secure share or provide a secure link.

4) Logging/retention controls and encryption:
- Retention windows are configurable; for Dedicated/Private we can set retention to zero or a very short window and disable telemetry collection for your project.
- Customer-managed KMS is available for disk and object storage encryption.

Next steps (technical):
- Marissa/Legal: if you can review the attached BAA and indicate edits, we can exchange via DocuSign (link below).
- Tech sync: I'll set up a 30-min call to walk through network, KMS, and logging options. Please include your security architect.

References & links:
- Security questionnaire (initial) attached: ShieldSec_Security_Q_initial.pdf
- DocuSign BAA link: https://app.docusign.com/BAA/Redwood-BAA-DEAL-4721

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
